optionalSupplies: Clipboard or book to lean on
substitutes: No paper? Draw on the back of an envelope or the inside of a cereal box flap.
title: The Edge of the Map
clue: Somewhere near here the map you carry in your head simply stops.
reveal: Draw the edge of your dog's usual world, then walk to it and extend the frontier by exactly one corner. Whatever is round that corner gets added to the map. Next week, there is another corner.
objective: Draw your usual walking map, step one corner past its edge at your dog's pace, then redraw the frontier.
instructions: Take a sheet of paper and a pencil. Draw your front door in the middle, then trace the streets you walk most often. Shade where the familiar stops: this is the Edge of the Map.

Pick one frontier corner: the nearest street end or path just past the Edge that you can see is safe in daylight, with sidewalk, no new road to cross and nothing steep. Mark it with a small cross on your map.
Walk to the Edge by the usual route at the usual pace. Stop there, loosen the leash, say "Edge of the map" and wait a few quiet seconds. This is the pause before the unknown.

Offer the corner: stand still and see whether your dog looks, leans or steps toward the new street. Follow if they do. If they hesitate or turn for home, that is information, not failure: look down the new street from where you stand and the corner still counts as seen.

Walk to the next corner only, let your dog sniff the new street for as long as they like, then turn around. One corner is the whole rule: the unknown stays close and you stay in charge of the turnaround.
Back home, redraw the Edge one corner further in a different color. Name the new street whatever your dog's reaction suggests: Windy Lane, Hedge Row, The Big Smell. Sign it with a drawn paw print.
Keep the map. When you want another adventure, start from the new Edge.
twist: Each trip extends the map by only one corner, so the unknown is always close, and the sheet becomes a record of your dog's slowly growing world.
variations: Doorstep frontier, for a slow, senior or nervous dog: the Edge is the end of the sidewalk outside your door, and looking down the next street from the corner counts.
Home Country, for a puppy not yet cleared for public places or a new dog: draw your apartment or yard, make the Edge the last room or flower bed your dog visits, and extend by one corner of it.

Become Regulars: instead of expanding, deepen. Visit one corner at the Edge at the same hour once a week for four weeks, with nothing to do but sit, sniff and notice (or revisit it each season). On week four set a handwritten RESERVED card on the mat as a joke, then pick it up. Nothing is promised: the spot may start to feel familiar, or not, and a week your dog would rather skip can be skipped.
Blind Pin: look at a local map or just think of your area, close your eyes, point, and make that the frontier corner, as long as it is safe, close and on a route you can walk.
completion: You have walked to the Edge, looked or stepped one corner past it, turned around and redrawn the map. If your dog said no, redrawing it with what you saw counts.
photoIdea: Your dog at the Edge corner looking down the new street, with the map held in the corner of the frame. Taken from behind, no calling.
memoryPrompt: What was round the corner that your dog had never seen?
safety: Sidewalk too hot for the back of your hand is too hot for paws; head home if your dog pants hard or shivers.
Keep your dog on a leash, follow local rules, and steer them away from glass and dropped food.
Puppies: do the Home Country version until your vet says unfamiliar streets are fine.
